name: Undersea cables & GPS
value: Asia cable faults; Gulf/Baltic GNSS jamming
summary: Asian subsea cable faults under repair; GNSS jamming in Gulf and Baltic
state: A subsea link between the Philippines and Singapore failed in October, slowing internet services, with repairs expected to take weeks (Rappler). GNSS jamming remains widespread in the Gulf and Baltic. No new cable cut had been reported as of 3 Nov.
for_you: No action needed; some services in affected regions may be slower.
rubric_hit: Cable damage; widespread GNSS interference = Watch

sources.title: Rappler — Subsea cable cut between Philippines and Singapore
Hellenic Shipping News — GPS jamming now a mainstream maritime threat

why: Subsea cables carry ~99% of intercontinental data; GPS jamming affects aviation and shipping.
drivers: Anchor drags, sabotage, conflict-zone jamming and spoofing.

rubric.alert: Multiple cable cuts isolating a region, or confirmed sabotage.
rubric.watch: Cable damage incident, or widespread GNSS interference affecting aviation.
rubric.normal: No new cable cuts or major jamming escalations.
